channel.description: Latest articles from MediaToday Co Ltd (maltatoday.com.mt)

item.title: 15% increase in student stipends takes effect tomorrow
item.description: Around 16,600 students will receive higher payments from February 25, with government allocating €6 million for the uplift announced in the 2026 Budget

item.title: WATCH | PM denies claims of judicial interference: ‘I have full respect for Lawrence Mintoff and judiciary’
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela rejects claims he interfered in the work of the judiciary, insisting he has ‘full respect’ for Judge Lawrence Mintoff and will answer questions in the appropriate forum

item.title: IT technician cleared of child sex abuse material charges
item.description: Judgment calls for new legislation to protect data recovery professionals who may be exposed to serious criminal charges simply because unlawful material is found on devices they are servicing

item.title: Repubblika warns judicial appointments should not depend on political calculations
item.description: Civil society organisation Repubblika says saga surrounding appointment of chief justice shows need for constitutional reform

item.title: Pensioner charged with setting fire to his own car
item.description: Accused denied using the car for over a day but CCTV and investigations revealed he had made use of the car hours before the incident

item.title: Young tourist couple handed suspended sentences for drunken fight with each other
item.description: Two tourists who have been in a relationship for five months were handed suspended prison sentences after admitting to assaulting each other during a drunken argument in St Julian’s

item.title: Abela’s position is vulnerable after judge’s letter
item.description: The prime minister has to give a thorough explanation of his behaviour if he does not want his position to swiftly go from vulnerable to untenable

item.title: Malta’s neutrality tested: Five lessons from Ukraine
item.description: Four years on, the war in Ukraine has raised difficult questions for Malta’s foreign policy, which is rooted in respect for international law and neutrality. James Debono draws five lessons from the conflict

item.title: Malta cannot continue to overlook its growing loneliness crisis
item.description: The next step must be decisive, systemic and based on evidence. It must be taken now, rather than postponed for future generations

item.title: Unlocking potential in empty homes
item.description: By blending state support with private initiative, it aims to enhance social housing capacity, revitalise urban areas, and unlock the potential of long-unused residential stock
